lines.say: You lose ten kilos of fat. Where does it actually go?
In one survey, most doctors got this wrong. They said it turns into energy.
Here's the truth. Your fat sits inside fat cells, as droplets called triglycerides.
When you burn it, they break apart and ride your blood to cells like your muscles.
There, tiny engines called mitochondria burn them with oxygen.
And what comes out? Carbon dioxide... and water.
Of those ten kilos, eight point four leave through your lungs.
You literally breathe your fat out.
The last one point six leaves as water. Sweat, tears and pee.
So every time you're out of breath at the gym... that's your fat, leaving.
